profile.background: Math / CS background; Python and basic backtesting; several factor notebooks; no institutional quant internship. Need stronger evidence of research discipline, robustness and data quality.

trends.name: Research Reproducibility / Data QA
trends.note: Research teams value trustworthy pipelines and fast invalidation of bad results.

trends.name: Alternative Data Pipelines
trends.note: Useful but data access and licensing increase entry cost.

trends.name: Execution / Microstructure Tooling
trends.note: High technical depth and stronger systems differentiation.

trends.name: Generic Factor Backtests
trends.note: Easy to overfit and common in student portfolios.

wedge.name: Robustness-first Systematic Research
wedge.thesis: A reproducible research process with data QA, transaction costs, sensitivity analysis and failure regimes is harder to fake and more interview-defensible than another high-Sharpe notebook.
wedge.killCriteria: Target roles consistently prioritize low-level systems/C++ execution work and research-hygiene evidence does not improve interview traction.
wedge.nextTest: Take one simple factor and build a reproducible package with cost model, subperiod robustness, lag checks and failure-regime analysis.

proofs.name: Robust Factor Research Package
proofs.evidence: Config + research memo + experiment table + sensitivity outputs

claims.claim: Built a reproducible factor-research pipeline with transaction-cost and robustness checks
claims.evidence: Code; config; research memo; experiment table

claims.risk: Out-of-sample validity, costs and overfitting make this unsafe as a strong claim

position.safe: Quant-oriented researcher with reproducibility, data QA and robustness-first research habits.
position.stretch: Systematic research candidate able to turn a trading hypothesis into a defensible experiment with cost, sensitivity and failure-regime analysis.
position.gaps: Live execution; production infra; real risk management; deeper C++/systems evidence for some roles.

applications.next: Map research vs quant-dev expectations before applying
Share reproducible research memo rather than headline Sharpe

interview.risk: Any precise performance metric without robust methodology
interview.weakness: Backtest can be challenged on universe, costs, lags and data leakage.
interview.drill: What happens to the signal under delayed execution, higher costs, another subperiod and a slightly different universe?
